title: QRÖMELIFE
excerpt: Quavo has released *QRÖMELIFE*, his third solo album, a 14-track record developed with Pharrell Williams over more than a year and a half.
body:
Quavo has released *QRÖMELIFE*, his third solo album, a 14-track record developed with Pharrell Williams over more than a year and a half. It follows 2023's *Rocket Power*, but comes from a different point in his life. The grief surrounding Takeoff's death is still present, only now it sits beside reconciliation, fatherhood and a project built to move rather than remain in one emotional place.

Sessions moved between Louis Vuitton's headquarters in Paris and a yacht in Miami. Pharrell's role extended across the project, with the two working closely enough that the collaboration became part of its identity rather than a name added at the end. The aim was to put several sides of his music on the same project, from the melodic phrasing that became central to Migos to the Atlanta rhythms underneath it and the experiments that had often appeared on features or isolated solo tracks.

The title comes from his idea of a "qrome" state, a way of describing the point at which pressure, loss and difficult experiences become part of how a person carries himself instead of something that can simply be erased. Quavo has linked that idea directly to the years after Takeoff's death and to the work of getting through them without pretending the loss disappeared. Compared with *Rocket Power*, which was made much closer to the shock of 2022, *QRÖMELIFE* gives more space to faith, family, work and the life that continued around the loss. The songs spend less time revisiting the event itself and more time on the life around it.

[apple:album:6817200688]

The strongest link back to Migos arrives on "Away," which reunites Quavo and Offset on a new recording after years apart musically. Their return together matters without swallowing the rest of the project. The two have also confirmed that they are working on another Migos record intended to honor Takeoff, although no release date has been announced. On *QRÖMELIFE*, the reunion works as part of a solo album that already has its own direction rather than as a shortcut back to the group.

Fatherhood has changed that direction too. Quavo recently confirmed that he has become a father for the first time and introduced his daughter in a short film tied to the release. He has spoken about the new purpose and motivation she brought into his life. The film moves through older Migos footage, grief, studio work and the making of *QRÖMELIFE* before ending with father and daughter together, placing that private change beside the public history he is trying to carry forward.

The music itself is noticeably lighter on its feet than *Rocket Power*. "HAAVIN" first surfaced during the Louis Vuitton menswear show in Paris, while "Trance (Walk It Down)" pushes further toward the dance floor without dropping the clipped rhythms and melodic delivery associated with his Atlanta records. The shifts are wide enough to change the album's temperature from track to track, but they stay tied together by the same voice instead of turning the project into a roll call of styles or guests.

A 16-track extended version followed a day after the standard edition, adding two versions of "HOTEL LOBBY (Unc & Phew)" with Takeoff. Bringing that song into the expanded release reconnects the new chapter with one of Quavo and Takeoff's best-known records without changing the focus of the 14-track core album. *QRÖMELIFE* does not try to rebuild Migos or repeat the grief of *Rocket Power*. It catches Quavo at a point where the past remains visible, while reconciliation, fatherhood and a renewed creative partnership are beginning to carry equal weight.
